persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 9 July 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: Paul J. Carli is the only Carli the town documents at all, and `P. S. Carli` is printed in the same paper inside the same four months — 9 July and 10 September 1834 against his own 18 June and 8 October.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE SAME PAPER SETS BOTH MIDDLE INITIALS AND SETS THEM APART: `P. J. Carli` on 18 June 1834 stands on the Paul J. Carli card, and `P. S. Carli` is a second reading, twice, under a different letter. A compositor's slip would have to have been made twice and never made in the other direction. Nothing else is recorded of either — no trade, no address — so there is no evidence beyond the initials to settle it. R3.

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'carli_p_s:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('carli_p_s:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. carli_p_s, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e0234 (contested, so nothing crossed).
